correctness.summary: The stage indexing ensures every length-n_m window either crosses the separator or lies in weights at most h_m, while the plateau attains \(h_m^{n_m}\); the longer plateau gives exact equality at m n_m. Normalizing \(T^{n_m}\) therefore gives an m-th-power norm-one witness for every m. Decay of weights proves compactness and quasinilpotence, and the Schatten criterion is the standard diagonal singular-value calculation.

final_claim: Below every prescribed positive null envelope there is an injective compact quasinilpotent unilateral weighted shift whose generated radical algebra has unit-ball m-th-power modulus one for every \(m\ge2\); choosing an all-ell_p envelope makes the generator belong to every Schatten class without improving uniform topological nilpotence.

residual_risks: Older radical-Banach-algebra literature could contain an equivalent rate-prescription refinement under different terminology.
originality.summary: Peters–Wogen (1999) is decisive prior art for the qualitative weighted-shift obstruction and already uses normalized powers with a norm-one obstruction at every finite exponent along a fixed constructed sequence. The audited theorem does not claim that phenomenon as new: its stronger quantifier is domination by an arbitrary prescribed null envelope, yielding simultaneous membership in every Schatten class. Full inspection of Example 2.5 did not state this arbitrary-envelope strengthening, and Peters (2024) does not add it.

value.summary: The arbitrary-envelope strengthening isolates a natural operator-ideal boundary: even super-polynomial singular-value decay of the generator gives no uniform topological-nilpotence gain. This is a motivated negative structural statement about the interaction between compactness ideals and radical algebra power behavior, not merely a recomputation of the 1999 example.
